_about: Every number in this file is an ASSUMPTION unless a source is named next to it. Edit here, not in code. Loaded by hroute/config.py.

_sources._about: source_status: verified = a team member read the primary text; to_confirm = cited from research notes, primary not yet read. Numbers are unchanged until confirmed.

IRC_103_2012_kerb.text: IRC:103-2012 Guidelines for Pedestrian Facilities, cl. 6.2.1: maximum height of a pavement (including kerb, walking surface, top-of-paving) shall not exceed 150 mm from the road level (same 150 mm in IRC:103-2022 cl. 6.2)

IRC_103_2022.text: IRC:103-2022 (Guidelines for Pedestrian Facilities, 2nd revision), sec 6.7 'Painted Zebra Crossing', Fig. 48: kerb ramp 'should not be steeper than 1:15 and slope on flared sides should be 1:10'. Footpath/kerb height 150 mm: IRC:103-2022 cl. 6.2

MoHUA_HG_2021.text: MoHUA Harmonised Guidelines and Standards for Universal Accessibility in India 2021 (March 2022 print): kerb ramp max 1:12, flares max 1:10 (cl. 3.7.2); kerb ramp min width 900 mm (cl. 3.7.3); external ramps 1:12 only up to 6 m run, longer runs flatter (Table 3.4); walkway min width 1200 mm, 1800 mm for two-way (cl. 3.5.1; other copies number it 3.4.1, cite the edition)

IRC_older_speed.text: older pedestrian design speed about 0.79 m/s (IRC older guidance)
IRC_older_speed.note: second-hand via research digest 2.6; treat as an assumption until the code text is read

project_sidewalk_licence.text: Project Sidewalk label data: 'dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0' (sidewalk-chandigarh.cs.washington.edu/api, Data License & Provenance; cite the Project Sidewalk CHI 2019 paper). Their OSM-derived street geometry is ODbL. Our network is built from OSM, so maps attribute OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL)

_sources._rule: stricter-for-wheelchair = 1:15 (IRC:103-2022) over 1:12 (MoHUA HG 2021); always cite year/edition

network._about: road width estimates used to place generated sidewalks. offset = width/2 + kerb_to_walk_centre_m, clamped. ASSUMPTION, Indian urban defaults, overridden by OSM width or lanes tags.

attach._about: barrier placement model. p(segment) proportional to distance x bearing x side x kind prior; a null 'off-network' candidate keeps p honest.

profiles._about: speed_mps: ASSUMPTION for every profile. walker_elderly 0.79 m/s follows an IRC older-pedestrian design value (source_status to_confirm, see _sources.IRC_older_speed). unknown_penalty_s: expected extra seconds if an unseen barrier is met.

manual_wheelchair.label: Manual wheelchair
manual_wheelchair.slope_rule: stricter of MoHUA HG 2021 cl. 3.7.2 (1:12) and IRC:103-2022 sec 6.7 (1:15) => 1:15

power_wheelchair.label: Power wheelchair
power_wheelchair.slope_rule: stricter of MoHUA HG 2021 cl. 3.7.2 (1:12) and IRC:103-2022 sec 6.7 (1:15) => 1:15 for all wheelchairs

unknown_prior._about: ASSUMPTION: chance an unseen barrier that matters sits on a segment with no clear evidence. linear kinds: p = 1-(1-per_100m)^(length/100); short kinds: p = per_segment. cost = -ln(1-min(p,0.99)) x profile unknown_penalty_s. Only clear-type evidence (seen and fine) removes it, and only within clear_radius_m of the label.

_block_p_about: a blocking barrier counts as a hard block when p_present >= block_p; below it, it adds p * soft_block_cost_s instead

barriers._about: per barrier type, per profile: block (hard) or cost_s (seconds added, times p_present). height rules: block_if_height_cm_gt; unknown_height = block|cost. ASSUMPTION except where a source is named.

missing_footpath._about: walking in the carriageway with traffic

pole_obstruction._about: clear width unknown from a point label; a measured clear_width_cm < 90 blocks wheelchairs (MoHUA min 1200 mm path)

steep_slope._about: extension type (not in the B1 label set): handled by slope rules in profiles; cost_s here is for slope above the profile's slope_cost_from_pct

_clear_types_about: positive evidence: the segment was seen and this was fine. Counts as verified, never as 'safe'.

temporal._about: temporary barriers: p_present = confidence x min(1, max(decay, recurrence) x hour_ratio). decay = 0.5^(hours since observed / half_life_h). hour_ratio = curve[leave hour] / max(curve[observed hour], 0.1). All ASSUMPTIONS: no Indian hourly survey of vendors or footpath parking was found.
temporal.permanent_note: permanent barriers do not decay; their age is reported so a stale photo is visible

source_tiers._about: what_if records are placed by the routing lane to demonstrate profile and leave-time effects; they cost like real barriers but never count as evidence

kind_block._about: segment kinds a profile cannot use at all. median = generated median/island side of a dual carriageway or roundabout, no footpath assumed (ASSUMPTION)

_dedupe_about: same-type barrier labels within dedupe_m on one segment are one cluster (p = max); clusters of one type combine as 1-prod(1-p), so a type costs at most its cost_s once per segment
